newsitem.title: ESTONIA: CENTRAL BANK TO RAISE CAPITAL ADEQUACY LEVEL.
newsitem.headline: CENTRAL BANK TO RAISE CAPITAL ADEQUACY LEVEL.

text.p: The central bank said on Wednesday that it has decided to increase the capital adequacy ratios of commercial banks from eight percent to 10 percent.
The bank said in a statement that the new ratios would come into force from October 1.

The bank said that the new capital adequacy rules would decrease the stimulus for banks to gain competitive advantage by taking additional risks and increased the protection of clients deposits and other claims.
The establishment of stricter rules compared to international minimum requirements was in line with the experience of many other transition economies, the bank added.
The bank also said it would make changes in the way it calculates capital adequacy and compulsory reserves.
Although the main target is to decrease the structural differences, they will also have a tightening affect on banks' expansion plans, the bank added.
The bank said it saw the requirements as way to secure the banking sector in the context of the goverment's plans to strengthen overall fiscal discipline.
The budget deficit and the deficit in the current account might become an important risk factor in the economy development, the bank added.
The bank said it fully supported the government's plans to continue conservative budget discipline and strengthen the budget discipline of local governments.
